statement: Prove that $\dfrac{\sin A+\sin B}{\cos A+\cos B}=\tan\dfrac{A+B}{2}$.
solution:
Using the sum-to-product identities,
$$\sin A+\sin B=2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2},\qquad \cos A+\cos B=2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}.$$
Therefore
$$\frac{\sin A+\sin B}{\cos A+\cos B}=\frac{2\sin\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}}{2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\cos\frac{A-B}{2}}=\tan\frac{A+B}{2},$$
provided $\cos\frac{A-B}{2}\neq0$ and the denominator is non-zero.
